events.name: Cal football vs Stanford: the 129th Big Game
events.details: rivalry game, the biggest home crowd of the season; listed on the official Cal schedule and the ESPN schedule feed

plan.audience: A mix of Cal students (18-22) who mostly walk from campus and nearby housing, plus older alumni, families and Bay Area locals who come by BART to Downtown Berkeley, by AC Transit, rideshare or car. A visiting Stanford contingent comes mostly by car from the Peninsula, with some taking BART from San Francisco or the Peninsula.
plan.attendance_reason: There is no sourced crowd figure, so this number is a default. The Big Game is Cal's biggest home draw of the season, but home Big Games in recent seasons have not reliably filled the 62,467 seats. A near-full crowd of about 56,000 is the central default. Capacity remains the upside case.
plan.reference_reason: Same stadium, same station, same 20-25 minute uphill walk and almost no parking, and the same college football crowd. The night series fits the post-game exit better: the game ends after dark around 20:00. The 16:30 Saturday kickoff means arrivals happen in daylight, so the day series informs the arrival shape.
multiplier_reasons: Parking: parking is already scarce in every DBRK reference game. A larger-than-usual crowd overwhelms the few lots and street spaces, pushing some extra drivers to BART. This is a modest increase, not a large one.
Walk: the walk is identical to the reference (20-25 min uphill from Downtown Berkeley), so it is neutral.

Crowd type: the rivalry draws more alumni, families and regional fans than a typical Cal home game, and these groups are more likely to ride BART than students. Stanford fans mostly drive, which offsets part of this.

Competing transit: as in the reference games, AC Transit, rideshare and walking from campus compete. BART is the main regional rail link, but there is no reason it gains more here than in the reference.

Time of day: arrivals happen on a Saturday midday to afternoon, with weekend train frequencies. Departures happen after dark, which favours BART over a long walk or bus wait, so this is slightly positive. The light rain may also tip a few walkers toward transit.
plan.arrival_reason: This is an even blend of the DBRK day and night arrival curves. The kickoff is at 16:30 on a Saturday, so fans arrive in daylight over the 12:00-16:00 window, with rivalry tailgating adding early arrivals. The 20-25 min walk means most riders tap out one to three hours before kickoff, and few arrive after the start hour.
plan.end_reason: A 16:30 kickoff plus the typical runtime of about 3h20-3h30 for a televised college game puts the final whistle near 19:50-20:00. This is well before BART's last trains.
plan.departure_reason: The game ends after dark, so the night DBRK exit pattern, with a sharp peak in the hour after the end hour, is the better guide. The specialist's even day/night blend folded the day series' late +3/+4 lingering into +2. That lingering reflects afternoon games followed by evening plans. A cold, drizzly November night favours prompt departures. Some celebration in downtown Berkeley keeps a moderate +2 share.
plan.weather_reason: Only about 0.4 mm of rain falls around the game (1.5 mm over the day), with a high of 12.3 C and moderate wind. That might cause a few no-shows among casual and family ticket holders, but committed rivalry fans attend. The effect on this event is small.
